resources.string: Share a file with a clone
No clones yet.\n\nTap “Clone an app” and pick one — WhatsApp, TikTok, or any app you use twice.

A work profile is a separate, private space on the same phone. Apps cloned into it keep their own login, their own chats, and their own notifications. In the app list they carry a small briefcase badge, so you can tell the clone from the original.

Android will say an organisation will manage this profile. That “organisation” is this app, on your own phone. Nothing is sent anywhere, no one else can see the profile, and you can delete it any time from Settings.
Some phones stop background apps to save power, which also stops clone notifications. Open the battery settings and allow App Cloner to run in the background. On Xiaomi phones this step matters most.
Allow notifications so a clone can tell you about a new message without opening this app.
Android’s own setup screen runs now. Read it and accept — the profile is created on your phone, and nothing leaves it.
What App Cloner cannot do — read the limits
Only apps with a home screen icon are listed. System apps are listed too, but most of them are not worth cloning.
This clone is frozen: it does not run and sends no notifications. Unfreeze it to use it again.

Work profile clones are real installs.

Notifications arrive normally, and banking apps work in a clone, because the clone is a genuine second install of the same app — not a trick copy.

Sandbox clones (coming in V2) are different: banking will not work in a sandbox, and notifications may arrive late, because the sandbox cannot pass the checks banks rely on.

No promise of 100 live accounts.

One phone can hold a few copies. A hundred accounts on one phone gets noticed and banned by the apps themselves. V1 allows 2 clones.

Proxy is off by default.

A proxy is an advanced option for V2 only, and it does not hide the phone — a proxy can leak the real address, so it is never sold as protection.

Updates do not break clones.

A clone is a separate install, so updating the original app leaves the clone alone. If a clone ever stops opening after an update, open its detail screen and re-clone it.

Some apps refuse a second copy.

Google apps, WhatsApp, YouTube, Snapchat and OneDrive check for this and may refuse to run cloned. That is their decision, not a bug in this app — the Limits list is kept up to date in the README.
